title: 2021 Fall AMC 12A Problem 14
statement: In the figure, equilateral hexagon \(ABCDEF\) has three nonadjacent acute interior angles that each measure \(30^\circ.\) The enclosed area of the hexagon is \(6\sqrt{3}.\) What is the perimeter of the hexagon?

solutions.text:
Let the common side length be \(s.\) The three acute vertices are the tips of isosceles triangles with two sides \(s\) and apex \(30^\circ;\) each has area \(\tfrac12 s^2 \sin 30^\circ = \tfrac{s^2}{4}.\)

The three reflex vertices form an inner equilateral triangle with side \(2s\sin 15^\circ,\) whose area is \(\sqrt3\,s^2\sin^2 15^\circ.\) Using \(\sin^2 15^\circ = \tfrac{2 - \sqrt3}{4},\) the total area is \[ \frac{3s^2}{4} + \sqrt3\,s^2\cdot\frac{2 - \sqrt3}{4} = \frac{s^2\sqrt3}{2}. \]

Setting \(\tfrac{s^2\sqrt3}{2} = 6\sqrt3\) gives \(s^2 = 12,\) so \(s = 2\sqrt3\) and the perimeter is \(6s = 12\sqrt3.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Let the side be \(s.\) The three \(30^\circ\) tips are isosceles triangles with legs \(s;\) they sit on the sides of the inner triangle formed by the three reflex vertices
Each tip has area \(\tfrac12 s^2 \sin 30^\circ,\) and the inner equilateral triangle has side \(2s\sin 15^\circ\)
